A Shell link is a data object that contains information used to access another object in the Shell's namespace, that is, any object visible through Windows Explorer. When the user creates a shortcut by choosing the Create Shortcut command, Windows stores the information in a link file, a binary file that has the .lnk file name extension.

Think before you Click(Fix): Analyzing the ClickFix social engineering technique. Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 21 August 2025. The ClickFix technique attempts to trick users into running malicious commands by taking advantage of human verification and CAPTCHA checks. It typically gives instructions that involve clicking prompts and copying, pasting, and running commands directly in the Windows Run dialog box, Windows Terminal, or Windows PowerShell. Because ClickFix relies on human intervention, organizations can reduce the impact by educating users and by hardening device configuration, for example disallowing the Run dialog when it is not needed.
